title: What is prayer?
summary: Why we pray, what prayer is in the Orthodox tradition, and how to begin without overcomplicating it.
intro:
Prayer is not, first of all, asking God for things. The Fathers describe prayer as standing in the presence of God. It is the lifting of the mind and heart to Him. To begin praying is simply to turn, even for a moment, away from the noise of the day and toward the One who is already with you.

St. Theophan the Recluse writes that the first task of prayer is attention: collecting the scattered mind and placing it in the heart. You do not need to feel anything dramatic. You do not need eloquent words. You only need to begin, and to keep beginning.

A good rule for the first weeks: keep your prayer short, regular, and from the heart. Two minutes morning and evening, prayed sincerely, are worth more than an hour of distracted recitation.
tryThis: Stand for one minute in silence before God this morning and evening. Say nothing. Simply remember that you are in His presence.

title: The Sign of the Cross
summary: How and why Orthodox Christians make the Sign of the Cross, finger by finger and shoulder to shoulder.
intro:
The Sign of the Cross is the oldest Christian prayer. Tertullian, writing around the year 200, says Christians make it at every turn of daily life: when they rise, dress, eat, leave the house, light a lamp, lie down to sleep. By the third century it is already universal, taken for granted by everyone in the Church.

It is a prayer made with the body. The hand confesses one mystery, the four movements confess another.

**The hand**

Bring together the thumb and the first two fingers of the right hand, with their tips touching. Fold the last two fingers, the ring finger and the little finger, flat against the palm.

The three joined fingers confess the Holy Trinity: three Persons of one essence, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, equal in glory and undivided. The two folded fingers confess the two natures of Christ, divine and human, united in one Person without confusion and without separation. In a single gesture the hand professes the Trinity and the Incarnation, the entire heart of the Faith.

**The four movements**

Touch the forehead, then the abdomen, then the right shoulder, then the left shoulder.

- The forehead, because Christ is the Head, and we offer Him the mind.
- The abdomen (not the chest), because He descended to the lowest parts of the earth for our sake, and we offer Him the body.
- The right shoulder, because Christ sits at the right hand of the Father, and the right is the side of the sheep in the parable of the Last Judgment.
- The left shoulder, that we may be moved from the left to the right, from death to life.

As you trace the four movements, say silently or aloud: "In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit." Then lower the hand and say "Amen," often joined with a small bow.

**When to make it**

Make the Sign of the Cross at every beginning and every end: when you rise, before you sleep, before and after meals, when you enter a church, when you pass an icon, when the Holy Name is spoken in prayer, when you bless yourself with holy water, when you are afraid, when you are grateful, when you do not know what to say. The ancient rule is simply this: at every step.

**Common mistakes to avoid**

- Making it from left to right. That is the Western practice. In the Orthodox East it is always right, then left.
- Using a vague waving motion or open palm rather than the proper position of the fingers.
- Hurrying. The Fathers say a quickly-made Sign is what the demons make at us, not what Christians make. Slow, attentive, full.
- Doing it absent-mindedly. The Sign is a prayer, not a habit. Make it consciously.

**The power of the Sign**

St. John Chrysostom writes that we ought never to leave the house without making this Sign, for in it is sealed our victory. The Fathers see the Cross of Christ standing behind every rightly-made Sign: the Trinity invoked, the Incarnation confessed, the Cross traced over the body that was bought with His blood.

It is not magic. It is faith made visible.
prayer: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
tryThis: Make the Sign of the Cross when you wake, before meals, before leaving the house, and before sleep. Slow and deliberate. Three fingers joined, two folded. Forehead, abdomen, right shoulder, left shoulder. Then "Amen" with a small bow.

title: The Jesus Prayer
summary: The short prayer that has carried Orthodox Christians for sixteen centuries.
intro:
"Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner."

This short prayer is the heart of Orthodox spirituality. It is named for the Lord whose Name is invoked. It can be prayed standing, walking, working, lying awake at night. The Fathers call it the prayer of the heart because, with time, it sinks from the lips to the mind, and from the mind to the heart.

St. Hesychios of Sinai writes that the Jesus Prayer is like a lamp in a dark room: as long as it burns, the room is full of light. Stop it, and the shadows return at once.

Do not strain to feel anything. Simply say the words, slowly, in time with your breath if that helps. Breathe in: "Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God," breathe out: "have mercy on me, a sinner." When your mind wanders, do not be discouraged. Bring it back. The bringing-back is half the work.
prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner.
tryThis: Pray the Jesus Prayer ten times this morning and ten times this evening. Slowly. Keep count on your fingers if you wish.

title: The Trisagion Prayers
summary: The opening prayers that begin every Orthodox prayer rule and most services of the Church.
intro:
The Trisagion ("thrice-holy") prayers are the doorway into Orthodox prayer. They are how every personal rule, and most public services, begin. They invoke the Holy Spirit, glorify the Trinity, and lead into the Lord's Prayer.

Learn them by heart over the next week. Once they are inside you, the rest of the prayer life unfolds easily.
prayer:
O Heavenly King, the Comforter, the Spirit of Truth, who art everywhere present and fillest all things, Treasury of good things and Giver of life: come and abide in us, cleanse us from every stain, and save our souls, O Good One.

Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us. (three times)

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

Most Holy Trinity, have mercy on us. Lord, cleanse us from our sins. Master, pardon our iniquities. Holy God, visit and heal our infirmities, for Thy Name's sake.

Lord, have mercy. (three times)

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy Name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.
tryThis: Read the Trisagion Prayers aloud, slowly, once a day for a week. Do not try to memorize. Familiarity will come on its own.

title: A simple morning rule
summary: A short morning prayer for beginners, drawn from the daily prayer of the Church.
intro:
A "prayer rule" is the small set of prayers you commit to saying every day at a fixed time. The point is not length, but constancy.

For a beginner, ten minutes in the morning is plenty. Stand facing east if you can, or facing your icons. Make the Sign of the Cross. Then pray the following.
prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.

O Heavenly King, the Comforter, the Spirit of Truth, who art everywhere present and fillest all things, Treasury of good things and Giver of life: come and abide in us, cleanse us from every stain, and save our souls, O Good One.

Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us. (three times)

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

Most Holy Trinity, have mercy on us. Lord, cleanse us from our sins. Master, pardon our iniquities. Holy God, visit and heal our infirmities, for Thy Name's sake.

Lord, have mercy. (three times)

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy Name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.

Rising from sleep, I thank Thee, O Holy Trinity, for through Thy great goodness and patience Thou wast not wroth with me, an idle and sinful one, neither hast Thou destroyed me with my iniquities, but hast shown Thy customary love for mankind, and hast raised me up as I lay in heedlessness, that I might sing my morning hymn and glorify Thy might.

Do Thou now enlighten the eyes of my mind, open my mouth to meditate on Thy words, to understand Thy commandments, to do Thy will, to sing to Thee in confession of heart, and to praise Thy most holy Name: of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

[Pray the Jesus Prayer slowly, ten times.]

Most holy Theotokos, save us.

It is truly meet to bless thee, O Theotokos, ever-blessed and most pure, and the Mother of our God. More honorable than the Cherubim, and more glorious beyond compare than the Seraphim, who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word: true Theotokos, we magnify thee.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

Lord, have mercy. (three times) Bless.

Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen.
tryThis: Pray this rule every morning for seven days. Keep it the same length each day. Do not skip and do not multiply.

title: A simple evening rule
summary: A short evening prayer for beginners, with examination of the day.
intro: Evening prayer turns the heart back to God before sleep, and offers Him the day that has passed. Stand before your icons, make the Sign of the Cross, and pray slowly. If the day was hard, this is the time to lay it down.
prayer:
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.

O Heavenly King, the Comforter, the Spirit of Truth, who art everywhere present and fillest all things, Treasury of good things and Giver of life: come and abide in us, cleanse us from every stain, and save our souls, O Good One.

Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, have mercy on us. (three times)

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy Name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.

O Lord our God, if I have sinned this day in word, deed, or thought, forgive me, for Thou art good and lovest mankind. Grant me peaceful and untroubled sleep. Send Thy guardian angel to protect and preserve me from every evil. For Thou art the Guardian of our souls and bodies, and unto Thee we ascribe glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

[A brief examination: bring to mind the day. Where did you fall short? Confess it briefly to God. Where did He bless you? Give thanks.]

[Pray the Jesus Prayer slowly, ten times.]

Into Thy hands, O Lord Jesus Christ my God, I commend my spirit. Bless me, save me, and grant unto me life eternal. Amen.

Most Holy Theotokos, save us.

It is truly meet to bless thee, O Theotokos, ever-blessed and most pure, and the Mother of our God. More honorable than the Cherubim, and more glorious beyond compare than the Seraphim, who without corruption gavest birth to God the Word: true Theotokos, we magnify thee.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

Lord, have mercy. (three times) Bless.

Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us. Amen.
tryThis: Before you close your eyes tonight, examine the day briefly. Confess what was sinful. Thank God for what was good. Then sleep in peace.
